en.html:
We stood before the Kyougoku residence.

The princess bowed her head, and we returned the courtesy.

What shamed me, honestly, was that my "we were of no use" had not even been modesty. It was just accurate. A humble man is supposed to push his achievement down a little. I had bent to push and found nothing there. Kya dabaoon? What was I to push down? We had brought her here by first bringing her everywhere else. Even the incompetence had taken the long route.

en.html:
There was a little hesitation in her voice.

Sakurako Okabe belonged to what remained of a warrior house that had raised arms against the shogunate, been branded traitors, and been destroyed.

For a person serving Rokuhara, friendship with her was not going to produce any advantage. For us also, supposed to be obedient little officials, the calculation was the same.

...Nevertheless, I nodded. Beside me, Ichijou nodded too.

en.html:
This was bad.

It had come without warning. Before I could stop her, the words were out.

Unforgivably rude, yes. But if that was all it sounded like—a Rokuhara official mocking someone defeated—still, it might pass.

Ichijou's feelings would not stay hidden. Anybody looking could see: she was not asking from the victor's side. She had gone over to the Okabe princess's side and was asking from there.

A shogunate official had no business standing in that place.

まずい。
　不意のことで、止め損ねた。

　あまりに無礼である――だが単なる無礼、六波羅の
役人の敗者への嘲弄と受け止められるなら、まだいい。
　しかし。

　一条は感情を隠せない。
　誰が見ても明らかだった。少女は勝者の立場で口に
していない。むしろ逆、岡部の姫の側に立って、問い
掛けている。

　断じて、幕府の役人のすべき事ではなかった。

en.html:
The princess herself could hardly have missed it. Confusion moved in her eyes.

Words to repair this, I had none. Nothing for it. I kept my face as unyielding as iron and watched without speaking.

Ichijou had lowered her gaze. Perhaps even she realized what she had said. What the princess saw in her, what conclusion she reached—I could not know.

When she spoke again, there was no color of emotion in the voice. Empty, however, it was not. Something firm was there.

en.html:
Sakurako"I am on the defeated side. Beyond that, I do not intend to say anything."
Ichijou"..."
Sakurako"We fought and lost. Now we keep silent and bow to the victor. That is the custom of a warrior house. Arguments must be made before the fighting starts. After defeat, fine speeches earn only the accusation of shamelessness."
Sakurako"I will not speak. From this mouth, nothing will come that shames the Okabe name. Not about Rokuhara... not about my father."
Sakurako"Not even... what was in my father's heart when he fought...!"
Kageaki"............"
Ichijou"..."
Ichijou"...I'm sorry..."
